guards.title: Escape inside the open access menu closes only the menu
guards.goal: The first Escape closes the menu and keeps the dialog open

plan.root_cause: The Escape key pressed on the access-toggle button is consumed by the dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler, which calls event.preventDefault() and event.stopPropagation() for Escape, preventing the modal's Escape listener from receiving the event and thus the share dialog does not close.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler to only preventDefault/stopPropagation for non‑Escape keys (ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space). This allows Escape to bubble up to the modal when the dropdown is not open, letting the modal close as expected while preserving dropdown-specific behavior for other keys.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Escape key will now close the share modal when focus is on the access toggle, allowing keyboard users to dismiss dialogs as expected.
functional_risks: Escape may also close the modal when the dropdown is open, potentially causing premature closure of both dropdown and modal.
If the modal's Escape handling is disabled (keyboard: false), the Escape will still bubble and may cause unintended side effects.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Escape with focus on the access-toggle button closes the share modal.
Verify that pressing Escape with the dropdown open closes the dropdown and returns focus to the toggle (does not close the modal unless intended).
Verify that ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter keys still operate correctly within the dropdown.
Verify that Escape still closes the modal when focus is elsewhere inside the modal (e.g., on Cancel or Save buttons).

plan.root_cause: The dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler handles the Escape key by closing the dropdown menu and focusing the toggle button, but does not call event.stopPropagation() when the dropdown is open. This allows the Escape event to bubble up to the modal's keydown listener, which then closes the modal and returns focus to the original trigger (#open-share) instead of keeping the modal open with focus on #access-toggle.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the Escape key handling block in dataApiKeydownHandler to call event.stopPropagation() when the dropdown is active (isActive === true). This prevents the event from reaching the modal handler while the dropdown is open, but still allows Escape to bubble to the modal when the dropdown is closed.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle (or within the open dropdown) will close only the dropdown and return focus to the toggle, keeping the share modal open. Pressing Escape when the dropdown is closed will bubble to the modal and close it as expected, returning focus to #open-share.
functional_risks: If isActive detection is incorrect (e.g., menu has 'show' class but dropdown is not truly open), stopPropagation may be called inappropriately.
The modal's Escape handler uses the 'keyboard' config option; if disabled, Escape would not close the modal anyway, but stopPropagation would still prevent any other Escape listeners.
verification_requirements: Verify Escape on #access-toggle with dropdown open closes dropdown only, focus returns to #access-toggle, modal stays open (#access-toggle visible).
Verify Escape on #access-toggle with dropdown closed closes modal, focus returns to #open-share.
Verify Escape on a dropdown item (e.g., #access-team) closes dropdown, focus returns to #access-toggle.
Verify ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter keys still operate correctly within the dropdown.
Verify Escape on Cancel (#share-cancel) or Save (#share-save) buttons closes the modal.

plan.root_cause: The dropdown's dataApiKeydownHandler unconditionally calls preventDefault() and stopPropagation() for the Escape key, even when the dropdown is closed. This prevents the Escape event from bubbling to the modal's keydown listener, so the modal does not close.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the handler to compute the dropdown's active state early. If Escape is pressed and the dropdown is not active, return without preventing default or stopping propagation, allowing the event to bubble to the modal. For all other cases (Escape when active, ArrowUp/Down, Space), prevent default and stop propagation as before.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape with focus on the access toggle (or anywhere in the modal when the dropdown is closed) will close the share modal and return focus to the trigger button. When the dropdown is open, Escape will close only the dropdown and return focus to the toggle, keeping the modal open.
functional_risks: If the dropdown's active state detection is incorrect (e.g., due to timing of class toggles), Escape might bubble when it shouldn't, or be prevented when it should bubble.

The modal's Escape handler relies on the 'keyboard' config option; if disabled, Escape would not close the modal anyway, but the dropdown would still not prevent propagation when closed (which is fine).
verification_requirements: Verify Escape on #access-toggle with dropdown closed closes modal, focus returns to #open-share.
Verify Escape on #access-toggle with dropdown open closes dropdown only, focus returns to #access-toggle, modal stays open.
Verify Escape on a dropdown item (e.g., #access-team) closes dropdown, focus returns to #access-toggle.
Verify ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Space, and Enter keys still operate correctly within the dropdown.
Verify Escape on Cancel (#share-cancel) or Save (#share-save) buttons closes the modal.
